verses.text: The whole group got up and brought Jesus to Pilate.
They began accusing him: “We caught this man turning the nation upside down, telling people not to pay Caesar’s taxes, and claiming he’s the Messiah—a king.”
Pilate asked Jesus, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “You said it.”
Pilate told the chief priests and the crowd, “I find no reason to charge this man.”
But they kept pushing: “He’s stirring up the people, teaching all through Judea, from Galilee right down here!”
When Pilate heard them mention Galilee, he asked if Jesus was a Galilean.
When he learned Jesus was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem at the time.
Herod was thrilled to see Jesus. He’d wanted to meet him for a long time after hearing all the stories, and hoped to see him do a miracle.
Herod questioned Jesus again and again, but Jesus didn’t answer.
The chief priests and law teachers stood there, fiercely accusing him.
Herod and his soldiers mocked and humiliated Jesus. They dressed him in fancy clothes and sent him back to Pilate.
That very day, Herod and Pilate became friends. Before this, they’d been enemies.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the leaders, and the people.
He said, “You brought this man to me, saying he was turning the people against you. I questioned him right here in front of you, and I found no basis for your charges.”
“Herod didn’t find anything either—I sent you to him. Jesus hasn’t done anything deserving death.”
“So I’ll have him beaten and then release him.”
At the festival, Pilate was supposed to release one prisoner to the people.
But they all shouted together, “Get rid of this man! Release Barabbas to us!”
Barabbas had been thrown in prison for starting a revolt in the city and committing murder.
Pilate spoke to them again, because he wanted to release Jesus.
But they shouted, “Crucify him! Crucify him!”
Pilate asked them a third time, “Why? What evil has he done? I found no crime deserving death. I’ll have him beaten and release him.”
But they kept shouting, louder and louder, demanding that Jesus be crucified. Their voices—and the chief priests’ voices—won out.
Pilate ruled that their demand should be carried out.
He released the man they had asked for, the one jailed for revolt and murder. But he handed Jesus over to their will.
As they led Jesus away, they grabbed Simon from Cyrene, who was coming in from the countryside, and put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
A huge crowd followed Jesus, including women who were mourning and crying for him.
Jesus turned to them and said, “Women of Jerusalem, don’t cry for me. Cry for yourselves and your children.”
“The days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the women who never had children, the wombs that never carried a baby, and the breasts that never nursed.’”
“Then they’ll beg the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and the hills, ‘Cover us!’”
“If this is what they do while the tree is green, what will happen when it’s dry?”
Two other men, both criminals, were being led out with Jesus to be executed.
When they reached the place called The Skull, they crucified Jesus there with the criminals—one on his right, the other on his left.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them; they don’t know what they’re doing.” Then the soldiers divided his clothes and rolled dice for them.
The people stood watching. The leaders sneered too: “He saved others! If he’s God’s Messiah, the Chosen One, let him save himself!”
The soldiers mocked him too. They came up and offered him sour wine.
They said, “If you’re the King of the Jews, save yourself!”
An inscription was placed above him in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
One of the criminals hanging there insulted Jesus: “Aren’t you the Messiah? Save yourself—and us!”
But the other criminal corrected him: “Don’t you fear God? You’re facing the same sentence.”
“We’re getting what we deserve for what we did, but this man hasn’t done anything wrong.”
Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”
Jesus told him, “I’m telling you the truth: today you’ll be with me in Paradise.”
It was about noon, and darkness covered the whole land until three in the afternoon.
The sun went dark, and the temple curtain split down the middle.
Jesus shouted loudly, “Father, I place my spirit in your hands!” After saying this, he died.
When the Roman officer saw what had happened, he praised God and said, “This man really was righteous.”
The crowds that had gathered to watch saw what happened, then went home beating their chests in grief.
Everyone who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed him from Galilee, stood at a distance and watched.
There was a man named Joseph, a member of the council. He was a good and righteous man.
He had not agreed with the council’s plan or what they had done. He was from Arimathea, a Judean town, and he was waiting for God’s Kingdom.
Joseph went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.
He took the body down, wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a tomb cut into rock, where nobody had ever been buried.
It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was about to begin.
The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph. They saw the tomb and how Jesus’ body was laid there.
Then they went back and prepared spices and perfumes. On the Sabbath, they rested, as the commandment required.
